_comment: 1.12.2 line against Had Enough Items (the JEI fork), running the standalone in-client UI test harness (uitest/1.12.2-forge, an independent ForgeGradle 7 legacy-mode Gradle build in this repository, shared by both 1.12.2 rows) through the three-stage pipeline config->build->test: jt resolves and pins, builds/reuses the JECh srg jar from the 1.12.0 checkout and compiles the harness build, then launches that build's runClient with the jars under test as -PjechJar/-PjeiJar — the row is picked by the JEI-line jar's own filename, the build stages no choice of its own. The mod entry is named 'jei' although the jar is HadEnoughItems: the standalone backend finds its -PjeiJar target among the env's mods by that name (uitest_pipeline.JEI_MOD_NAME), so a HEI row travels the same slot — the slug/pin below still resolve the HEI artifact. The client drives the scenarios itself and writes report.json, its captures and junit.xml before it quits itself; that is why the row declares no ready_when (stopping this client early would kill it mid-scenario and leave no report) and no world (the level asserted against is the one the harness's runner creates and pins itself). No gradle block: the harness build is the launch layer. Its selection is the smoke scenarios only (tag:smoke), unlike the legacy-JEI row: HEI answers through the IAdvancedSearchRegistry path (JechJeiPlugin.JechSearchIndex), not through the legacy suffix-tree replacement the JEI scenarios are written against, so this row claims what it was measured with rather than running scenarios it does not exercise. jech and the HEI jar both carry via=dev-classpath, each for its own measured reason: the JECh srg jar rides the run task's classpath, where FML's ModDiscoverer.findClasspathMods discovers the jecharacters mod in it and the dev run's FMLDeobfuscationTransformer maps its SRG member references into the run's MCP names at load time; the JEI-line jar has to be staged by the build itself with its access transformer remapped, because a published 1.12.2 AT is written in SRG member names that never match the MCP-named members a dev client has — a raw staged copy dies in JEI's own init with IllegalAccessError on TextureMap.initMissingImage (measured; the build's stageUiTestDevMod does the remap, fail-closed on a rule without an MCP name in its comment). The srg classifier is required on jech.path: the checkout's build directory also holds the non-srg jar, and only the srg one is a 1.12.2 runtime jar. java.version 21 is the JDK the harness build's Gradle wrapper itself runs on (Gradle 9.8.1 cannot start on the row's client JDK 8); the client stays on the build's own toolchain 8. With HEI the legacy GeneralizedSuffixTree constructor patch is not applied (that is the legacy-JEI path only), so that check is absent here. The narrative and the earlier measurements are in envs/README.md, 'The 1.12.2 rows and the gradle launch'.
